title: This Tiny Mining Town Is Said to Be One of the Most Haunted Places in the West—and It's the Perfect Spooky-season Getaway
excerpt: Once a rough-and-tumble copper-mining hub, Bisbee now pairs beautifully preserved architecture and bohemian charm with some seriously eerie local lore.
content:
Nicholas DeRenzo

Tue, September 22, 2026 at 5:20 PM UTC

Once a rough-and-tumble copper-mining hub, Bisbee now pairs beautifully preserved architecture and bohemian charm with some seriously eerie local lore.

Set about 100 miles southeast of Tucson, Arizona, and just 11 miles north of the Mexican border, the former copper-mining hub of Bisbee, Arizona, is full of surprises: the progressive, bohemian enclave stands apart from much of surrounding Cochise County—it became Arizona’s first municipality to approve a civil-union ordinance—and its rough-and-tumble frontier history has helped earn it a reputation as one of the most haunted towns in the West.

In other words, it’s the perfect place for a spooky-season weekend getaway.

Known for its well-preserved early 20th-century architectural landmarks, Bisbee is filled with so many alleged ghosts that selecting where to stay can feel a bit like a choose-your-own-spirit adventure. Opened in 1902 during the mining boom, the Copper Queen Hotel ranks as Arizona’s oldest continuously operating hotel and is said to be home to Julia Lowell, a sex worker who died by suicide; a young boy named Billy; and a cigar-smoking old man who hangs out on the fourth floor.

The Essential Guide to Bisbee

The 120-year-old Bisbee Grand Hotel, meanwhile, is believed to be haunted by a woman in Victorian dress who floats through guest rooms and leaves behind the scent of lilac and a spectral man who sticks to the saloon downstairs. And at Hotel La More at the Bisbee Inn, there are even tales of a “phantom feline” that skulks through room 23.

If you don’t feel like searching for ghosts on your own, there are a few different options for guided experiences: US Ghost Adventures offers an hour-long tour called Buried Beneath Bisbee: Rattlesnakes & Revenants Ghost Tour, which stops at a few haunted hotels and the Old Bisbee Jail and contextualizes the brawls, love triangles, and massacres that have led to so many restless souls sticking around the neighborhood. And Old Bisbee Ghost Tour offers a walking tour (you can rent ghost-hunting gear for an additional $5), an accessible drive via golf cart, and a pub crawl, with drinks at the newly opened Spirits Society.

For something completely different, check out the Object Hotel, which opened in 2018 inside a 1907 Italianate building on Main Street that once housed the town Woolworth’s. Today, it’s a collection of hotel rooms and furnished apartments owned by artist and footwear designer Rachel Brand that’s perfect for both short- and longer-term stays and extended remote work for creatives. This spring, the Tucson-based Nexus Occult Books & Oddities opened a pop-up outpost at the Object, with more than 1,800 books on the occult, while the nearby Bell, Book & Candle is a “tiny magical shop” stocked with tarot cards and hand-poured candles.
